title: Account and security
summary: Your password, two-step verification, passkeys, recovery codes, signing out, and the extra check for Health and Finances.

blocks.title: Where to click
items: On the sign-in page, press **Forgot password?**.
Type your email and press **Send reset link**.
Open the link in the email (it works for 60 minutes) and choose a new password.

blocks.text: A good password has at least 12 characters. A long sentence is easier to remember than random symbols. After you set a new password you are signed out on your other devices.

sections.title: Two-step verification with an authenticator app

blocks.text: Two-step verification asks for a short code from your phone, as well as your password. It protects your account if somebody learns your password. The administrator may require it before you open Health or Finances.

blocks.title: Where to click
items: Install an authenticator app on your phone, if you do not have one.
Open the account menu, choose **Settings**, then **Security**.
Scan the QR code with the app. If you cannot scan, press **Can't scan? Enter the key instead** and type the key.
Type the 6-digit code the app shows and press **Confirm code**.
Save your recovery codes (see below), tick **I have saved these codes somewhere safe**, and press **Finish setup**.

blocks.text: When you sign in, the app asks for the 6-digit code after your password. To turn the authenticator app off, use **Turn off authenticator app** in the same place.
A passkey lets you confirm it's you with your fingerprint, your face or your screen lock, instead of a code. It stays on your device.

blocks.title: Where to click
items: Press **Add passkey** and follow the prompt of your device.
Give the passkey a name, for example iPhone or Work laptop, and press **Save name**.

blocks.text: You can **Rename** or **Remove** a passkey later. If you see that your browser or device does not support passkeys, use an authenticator app instead.
Recovery codes are your emergency key. If you lose your phone, a recovery code lets you sign in. Each code works only once. The app shows them only at setup.

items: Save them in a safe place: copy or download them, or write them on paper.
Security shows how many codes are left. When few are left, press **Create new codes**. Old codes then stop working.
If you have no codes and no phone, ask your administrator to reset your two-step verification.

blocks.text: Choose **Log out** in the account menu to sign out on the device you are using. If you lose a device, change your password with **Forgot password?**: this signs you out everywhere. The administrator can also sign you out on a device you no longer have.
If you signed in on a shared computer and forgot to log out, change your password as soon as you can.

sections.title: Confirm it's you, and the lock for Health and Finances

blocks.text: Health and Finances hold private data, so the app protects them more. After a period of inactivity, the app asks you to confirm it's you before it shows them again. It may also ask before sensitive actions, such as changing your security settings.

blocks.title: Where to click
items: When the **Confirm it's you** window appears, type your password, or use your passkey or authenticator code.
Then carry on. If an action was interrupted, repeat it.

blocks.text: The administrator can change how long this takes in Settings > Security. This is normal and not a sign that anything is wrong.
Save your work before you step away. Unsaved text in Health can be lost when the page locks.
